authoredSolutions.1: The horizontal launch speed was lost from the printed stem; the only value consistent with the options is \(u_x = 5\text{ }ms^{-1}\). Vertically the stone starts from rest and falls \(h = 10\text{ }m\), so \[v_y^2 = 2gh = 2\times 10\times 10 = 200\text{ }m^2s^{-2}.\] The horizontal component is unchanged, \(v_x = 5\text{ }ms^{-1}\), so \[v = \sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2} = \sqrt{25+200} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ }ms^{-1}.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.2: The figure shows two parallel infinite sheets, each carrying the SAME positive surface density \(+\sigma\). A single infinite sheet produces \(\dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\) pointing away from it on both sides. Take \(\widehat{n}\) directed from region I towards region III. In region I both sheets push to the left, giving \[{\overrightarrow{E}}_{I} = -\frac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\widehat{n}-\frac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\widehat{n} = -\frac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}\widehat{n}.\] In region II the two contributions are opposite and equal, so \({\overrightarrow{E}}_{II}=0\). In region III both point along \(+\widehat{n}\), giving \(\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}\widehat{n}\). Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.3: Volume is conserved, so \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 125\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), giving \(r = R/5\). The change in area is \[\Delta A = 125\left(4\pi r^2\right)-4\pi R^2 = 4\pi R^2\left(\frac{125}{25}-1\right)=16\pi R^2.\] Therefore \[\Delta E = T\,\Delta A = 0.45\times 16\pi\times\left(10^{-3}\right)^2 = 2.26\times 10^{-5}\text{ }J.\] Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.4: With \(M_E = 9M_P\) and \(R_E = 2R_P\), \[v_P = \sqrt{\frac{2GM_P}{R_P}} = \sqrt{\frac{2G\left(M_E/9\right)}{R_E/2}} = \sqrt{\frac{2GM_E}{R_E}}\sqrt{\frac{2}{9}} = \frac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{2}.\] Comparing with \(\frac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{x}\) gives \(x=2\). Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.5: For an adiabatic change \(TV^{\gamma-1}\) is constant with \(\gamma = 3/2\), so \[T_2 = T\left(\frac{V}{2V}\right)^{1/2} = \frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}.\] For one mole \[W = \frac{R\left(T_1-T_2\right)}{\gamma-1} = \frac{R}{1/2}\left(T-\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 2RT\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = RT\left[2-\sqrt{2}\right].\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.6: Since \(b\) is subtracted from \(V\), \([b]=\left[L^3\right]\). Since \(a/V^2\) is added to \(P\), \[[a]=\left[PV^2\right]=\left[ML^{-1}T^{-2}\right]\left[L^{6}\right]=\left[ML^{5}T^{-2}\right].\] Therefore \[\frac{\left[b^2\right]}{[a]}=\frac{\left[L^{6}\right]}{\left[ML^{5}T^{-2}\right]}=\left[M^{-1}L\,T^{2}\right],\] which is the reciprocal of \(\left[ML^{-1}T^{-2}\right]\), the dimension of bulk modulus. So it is the dimension of compressibility. Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.7: Reading the figure, the arms from \(A\) are \(R\) (upper) and \(2R\) (lower), meeting \(3R\) and \(6R\) respectively at \(B\), with \(9R\) bridging the two middle nodes. The bridge is balanced because \[\frac{R}{2R}=\frac{3R}{6R}=\frac{1}{2},\] so no current flows through \(9R\) and it may be removed. Then \[R_{eq}=\frac{(R+3R)(2R+6R)}{(R+3R)+(2R+6R)}=\frac{4R\times 8R}{12R}=\frac{8}{3}R.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.8: An AC generator works on electromagnetic induction, so A matches II. A transformer works on mutual induction, so B matches IV. Resonance requires both an inductor and a capacitor, so C matches I. The sharpness of resonance is measured by the quality factor, so D matches III. This gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III. Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.9: Let \(AB = BC = x\). Since \(AD = 3AB = 3x\), the third segment is \(CD = 3x-2x = x\), so all three segments are equal. Then \[\langle v\rangle = \frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}} = \frac{3x}{\dfrac{x}{v_1}+\dfrac{x}{v_2}+\dfrac{x}{v_3}} = \frac{3}{\dfrac{1}{v_1}+\dfrac{1}{v_2}+\dfrac{1}{v_3}} = \frac{3v_1v_2v_3}{v_1v_2+v_2v_3+v_3v_1}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.10: Unpolarised light loses half its intensity at the first sheet, and each of the remaining \(n-1\) sheets multiplies the intensity by \(\cos^2 45^{\circ}=\tfrac{1}{2}\). Therefore \[I_{out} = \frac{I}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} = \frac{I}{2^{n}}.\] Setting \(I_{out}=I/64=I/2^{6}\) gives \(2^{n}=2^{6}\), so \(n=6\). Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.11: Microwaves are produced by a klystron valve, so A matches IV. Gamma rays come from radioactive decay of the nucleus, so B matches I. Radio waves are produced by rapid acceleration and deceleration of electrons in aerials, so C matches II. X-rays involve inner shell electrons, so D matches III. This gives A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III. Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.12: Equal de Broglie wavelengths mean equal momenta, since \(\lambda = h/p\). For a non-relativistic particle \(K = \dfrac{p^{2}}{2m}\), so with the same \(p\), \[\frac{K_{p}}{K_{\alpha}} = \frac{m_{\alpha}}{m_{p}} = \frac{4m_p}{m_p} = 4.\] (The proton speed \(0.1c\) gives \(\gamma \approx 1.005\), so the non-relativistic treatment is accurate to better than one percent.) The required ratio of proton to alpha kinetic energy is therefore \(4:1\). Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.13: The time was lost from the stem; the value that makes the data consistent is \(t = 10\text{ }s\). Starting from rest, \[s = \tfrac{1}{2}at^{2}\ \Rightarrow\ 50 = \tfrac{1}{2}a(10)^{2}\ \Rightarrow\ a = 1\text{ }ms^{-2}.\] Newton's second law along the surface gives \[F-\mu mg = ma\ \Rightarrow\ 30-\mu(5)(10) = 5(1),\] so \(50\mu = 25\) and \(\mu = 0.50\). Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.14: Statement I is true: \(g\) varies over the earth's surface because the earth is not a perfect sphere and because of rotation, so \(g\) is larger at the poles than at the equator. Statement II is false: below the surface \[g_{d} = g\left(1-\frac{d}{R}\right),\] which decreases with depth and vanishes at the centre. Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.15: The FM broadcast band extends from about \(88MHz\) to \(108MHz\). Of the values listed, \(89MHz\), \(99MHz\) and \(106MHz\) all lie inside this band, while \(64MHz\) lies below it. Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.16: The helium nucleus has two protons and two neutrons, so the mass defect is \[\Delta m = 2(1.0073)+2(1.0087)-4.0015 = 2.0146+2.0174-4.0015 = 0.0305\ u.\] Using \(1u \equiv 931\ MeV\), \[B.E. = 0.0305\times 931 = 28.4\ MeV.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.17: The tension was lost from the stem; the value consistent with the options is \(T = 70\text{ }N\). The transverse wave speed on a stretched string is \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{70}{7.0\times 10^{-3}}} = \sqrt{10^{4}} = 100\text{ }m/s.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.18: In an intrinsic semiconductor the Fermi level lies midway between the valence and conduction bands, so A matches II. Donor doping in an n-type semiconductor raises the Fermi level towards the conduction band, so B matches III. Acceptor doping in a p-type semiconductor lowers it towards the valence band, so C matches I. In a metal the Fermi level lies inside the conduction band, so D matches IV. This gives A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV. Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.19: Reading the figure: the incoming straight wire is horizontal and tangent to the top of the circle, so \(P\) lies at perpendicular distance \(r\) from it, level with its end. The outgoing straight wire runs vertically downward from the bottom of the circle, and \(P\) lies ON the line of that wire, so it contributes nothing. The semicircle gives \[B_{arc} = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4r},\] and the semi-infinite horizontal wire, with \(P\) on the perpendicular through its end, gives \[B_{wire} = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}.\] Both are directed out of the page, so \[B = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4r}+\frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r} = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2r}\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2\pi}\right).\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.20: From kinetic theory the mean translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is \[\langle K\rangle = \frac{3}{2}k_{B}T,\] which depends only on the absolute temperature and not on pressure, volume or the identity of the gas. Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.21: The leading coefficient of the force was lost from the stem; the force is \(\overrightarrow{F} = 5\widehat{i}+2\widehat{j}+7\widehat{k}\text{ }N\). The displacement is \[\Delta\overrightarrow{r} = \left(5\widehat{i}-2\widehat{j}+\widehat{k}\right)-\left(2\widehat{i}+3\widehat{j}-4\widehat{k}\right) = 3\widehat{i}-5\widehat{j}+5\widehat{k}.\] Therefore \[W = \overrightarrow{F}\cdot\Delta\overrightarrow{r} = (5)(3)+(2)(-5)+(7)(5) = 15-10+35 = 40\text{ }J.\]
authoredSolutions.22: Bulk modulus is \(B = \dfrac{P}{\left|\Delta V/V\right|}\). The same pressure is applied to both, so \[\frac{B_{water}}{B_{liquid}} = \frac{\left|\Delta V/V\right|_{liquid}}{\left|\Delta V/V\right|_{water}} = \frac{0.03}{0.01} = \frac{3}{1}.\] Comparing with \(\dfrac{3}{x}\) gives \(x = 1\). (The stated volumes 1 litre and 2 litre are irrelevant because the compressions are quoted as fractional changes.)
authoredSolutions.23: The atom absorbs \(12.75\ eV\) from the ground state, so \[E_n = -13.6+12.75 = -0.85\ eV.\] Since \(E_n = -13.6/n^{2}\), \(n^{2} = 13.6/0.85 = 16\), giving \(n = 4\). authoredSolutions.24: Acceleration through \(\Delta V\) gives \(qV = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\), so \(p = mv = \sqrt{2mq\Delta V}\). In the field, \(r = \dfrac{p}{qB} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mq\Delta V}}{qB}\), so \[m = \frac{qB^{2}r^{2}}{2\Delta V} = \frac{\left(2\times 10^{-6}\right)\left(4\times 10^{-3}\right)^{2}\left(3\times 10^{-2}\right)^{2}}{2\times 100}.\] Evaluating, \[m = \frac{2\times 10^{-6}\times 1.6\times 10^{-5}\times 9\times 10^{-4}}{200} = 1.44\times 10^{-16}\text{ }kg = 144\times 10^{-18}\text{ }kg.\] Therefore the answer is 144.
authoredSolutions.25: The amplitude was lost from the stem; the value that gives an integer answer is \(A = 3\text{ }cm\). authoredSolutions.27: The focal length was lost from the stem; the value that gives an integer answer is \(f = 20\text{ }cm\) (so \(f = -20\text{ }cm\) with sign convention). authoredSolutions.91: At constant volume an ideal gas obeys \(P \propto T\) measured on the absolute scale, so each \(P\) versus \(t\left(^{\circ}C\right)\) line is straight. In the figure the three lines for gases A, B and C all extrapolate back to the SAME point \(K\) on the temperature axis, where \(P = 0\). authoredSolutions.92: An ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance; a real one is connected in parallel with the resistance being measured, and the higher its resistance the less current it diverts and the smaller the loading error. So for a \(600\Omega\) resistance the \(4000\Omega\) voltmeter is the better instrument, not the \(1000\Omega\) one, and Assertion A is INCORRECT. Reason R, that a voltmeter of higher resistance draws smaller current, is correct. Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.93: Impulse equals the area under the force-time graph. The largest area belongs to figure (b). Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.94: For a hydrogen-like atom \[\Delta E = 13.6\,Z^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_1^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right)\ eV\] with \(Z = 4\), \(n_1 = 2\), \(n_2 = 4\). authoredSolutions.95: For a plane electromagnetic wave the average electric energy density is \(\tfrac{1}{4}\varepsilon_0 E_0^{2}\) and the average magnetic energy density is equal to it, so the total average energy density is \(\tfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^{2}\). authoredSolutions.96: The radius of curvature was lost from the stem; the value consistent with the options is \(R = 40\text{ }cm\), so \(f = -20\text{ }cm\). authoredSolutions.97: Each of the \(n\) equal sides has resistance \(R/n\). Between two adjacent corners one side (\(R/n\)) is in parallel with the remaining \(n-1\) sides in series, \(\dfrac{(n-1)R}{n}\). Hence \[R_{eq} = \frac{\left(\dfrac{R}{n}\right)\left(\dfrac{(n-1)R}{n}\right)}{\dfrac{R}{n}+\dfrac{(n-1)R}{n}} = \frac{\dfrac{(n-1)R^{2}}{n^{2}}}{R} = \frac{(n-1)R}{n^{2}}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.98: With \(T_1 = 99^{\circ}C = 372\text{ }K\) and \(\eta = 1-\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \[T_2 = \frac{2}{3}\times 372 = 248\text{ }K.\] After raising the cold reservoir by \(x\), \[1-\frac{248+x}{372} = \frac{1}{6}\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{248+x}{372} = \frac{5}{6}\ \Rightarrow\ 248+x = 310,\] so \(x = 62\text{ }K\). authoredSolutions.99: For an isolated conducting sphere \(C = 4\pi\varepsilon_0 R\), which depends only on the radius. Charge resides entirely on the outer surface of a conductor, so a hollow and a solid sphere of the same radius have the same capacitance and therefore carry the SAME charge at the same potential, \(Q = CV\). Assertion A, which claims the solid sphere carries less charge, is false. Reason R, that the capacitance depends on the radius, is true. Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.100: Write \([M] = [G]^{x}[h]^{y}[c]^{z}\) with \[[G] = \left[M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2}\right],\quad [h] = \left[ML^{2}T^{-1}\right],\quad [c] = \left[LT^{-1}\right].\] Matching powers gives \(-x+y = 1\), \(3x+2y+z = 0\) and \(-2x-y-z = 0\), whose solution is \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\), \(y = \tfrac{1}{2}\), \(z = \tfrac{1}{2}\). authoredSolutions.101: A Zener diode is operated in REVERSE bias beyond its breakdown voltage, where a large change in current produces almost no change in voltage, which is exactly the behaviour needed for voltage regulation. In forward bias it conducts like an ordinary pn junction diode and offers no regulation. Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.102: The wire's length and cross-sectional area were lost from the stem; the printed paper gives \(L = 6\text{ }m\) and \(A = 3{\text{ }mm}^{2}\). authoredSolutions.103: The modulation index is \(\mu = \dfrac{A_m}{A_c}\). In the first case \(\mu_1 = \dfrac{X}{Y}\); in the second the carrier amplitude is doubled, so \(\mu_2 = \dfrac{X}{2Y}\).
